272:
Any person, firm, business, partnership, corporation or other entity licensed hereunder or patronizing an Adult Entertainment Business or Facility shall comply with the following rules and regulations:
1. No person shall offer Adult Entertainment and no Patron shall be or remain on the premises of any Adult Entertainment Facility except between the hours of 11:00 a.m. and 2:00 a.m. Monday through Friday, Saturday from 11:00 a.m. through 12:00 a.m. on Sunday, and Sundays between the hours of 12:30 P.M. and 12:00 Midnight.
2. No person under the age of eighteen (18) years shall be permitted on the premises of an Adult Entertainment Facility.
3. No Patron shall touch, fondle or caress any Employee, nor shall any Employee touch, fondle or caress any Patron.
4. No Patron shall place any tip or gratuity upon the person of any Employee or in the clothing of any Employee and no Employee shall permit any tip or gratuity to be placed on their person or in their clothing by a Patron.
5. All dancing by adult entertainers at Adult Entertainment facilities shall occur on a Fixed Stage. No part of any live performance of Adult Entertainment shall take place other than in an area generally accessible to all Patrons. No person who performs live Adult Entertainment shall leave a Fixed Stage during any performance, dance or demonstration.
6. No Patron shall be permitted on a Fixed Stage for any purpose.
7. No Patron seating shall be affixed or attached to a Fixed Stage.
8. No person shall serve, offer, consume or be in possession of any alcoholic beverage on the premises of an Adult Entertainment Facility or in any parking area dedicated to use of an Adult Entertainment Facility.
9. In all areas where Adult Entertainment occurs, lighting equivalent to five (5) foot candles, as that term is used in Kaufman and Christensen, Eds., IES Lighting Handbook (Illuminating Engineering Society of North American 1987), shall be maintained at all times that the Facility is open to Patrons.
10. No Adult Entertainment shall occur in a Private Room within an Adult Entertainment Facility.
11. No Patron shall be permitted to enter any Dressing Room or Private Room nor shall any Employee and Patron jointly occupy any Private Room or dressing area.
12. The License shall be displayed in a prominent place on the premises at all times.
13. Amateurs. No person who wishes to expose his or her Specified Anatomical Areas in any adult entertainment facility without being compensated or paid, shall do so without first applying for and receiving a work permit hereunder. A temporary or annual permit issued to any such amateur performer shall be governed by and subject to this Chapter as if the performer were an employee of the adult entertainment facility.
14. Consent to jurisdiction and service. Any licensee issued a license under this Chapter and any employee issued an work permit under this Chapter shall be deemed to have consented to the jurisdiction of the Municipal Court of the City of McDonough, Georgia, the State Court of Henry County, Georgia, and the Superior Court of Henry County, Georgia, for purposes of the enforcement of this Chapter, and shall also be deemed to have consented to service of any citation or summons issued under this Chapter via the United States mail with sufficient first class postage affixed and properly addressed to the licensee or employee at the address set forth on the application for such license or permit, as the case may be. Nothing herein shall be interpreted to preclude a police officer or deputy sheriff from personally serving a licensee or employee.
15. Covering of windows and doors. All adult entertainment which is licensed and permitted by this Chapter shall be carried on inside a closed building with all windows and doors covered so that the activities carried on inside cannot be viewed at any time from the immediate areas surrounding the outside of the building.
16. Retention of records. All adult entertainment facilities shall be required to retain all records pertaining to its employees for a period of ten (10) years, and such records shall be open to inspection by any city police officer for official police business during normal operating hours.
17. Cleaning of licensed premises. All adult entertainment facilities shall be kept in a clean, sanitary condition, and shall be in full compliance with all applicable ordinances and regulations of the City, Henry County, and the State of Georgia.
18. Inspection of licensed premises. City Code Enforcement officials, including the fire marshal and the City building code inspector shall have the authority to regularly inspect adult entertainment facilities, to determine compliance with and enforce all applicable fire, health and other codes of the City and Henry County.
19. Inspection for unsanitary or unsafe conditions. The City police department shall have the authority to inspect any adult entertainment facility at any time such facility is occupied by one (1) or more persons, in order to determine compliance with and enforce all provisions of this Chapter and other applicable ordinances, regulations and laws.
(Ord. No. 10-06-07(B), § I, 6-7-2010)
273:
An adult entertainment business shall designate in writing to the Chief of Police a person(s) to serve as an on-premises operator. The operator(s) shall be principally in charge of the facility and shall be located on the premises during all operating hours. If an adult entertainment business is found open for business without the presence of an on-premises operator, the licensee shall be cited for a violation of this Chapter, and the business shall be ordered to close until an on-premises operator is present and remains present during all operating hours.
(Ord. No. 10-06-07(B), § I, 6-7-2010)
274:
Adult Entertainment Businesses and Facilities shall be subject to the provisions of the Zoning Ordinance of the City of McDonough, Georgia, as may from time to time be amended, this Chapter, and the following standards of use:
1. In addition to the development standards of the Zoning Ordinance, each Adult Entertainment Business shall have a Facility dedicated solely to the operation of the Business named in its License. Said Facility shall be located on a lot used for no purpose other than the conduct of the Business named in the License. No Adult Entertainment Facility shall be located in any strip shopping center, mall or other group structure. No Adult Entertainment Facility shall share any common wall, parking area, entrance, waiting area, restrooms or lobby with any other business or use.
2. The minimum lot area for an Adult Entertainment Facility shall be one (1) acre.
3. In addition to zoning development standards governing zoning in the district of any proposed Adult Entertainment Business, buildings and structures established in connection with an Adult Entertainment Business (or as an Adult Entertainment Facility) shall be separated by at least forty (40) feet from the buildings and structures of any other business establishment. The minimum rear yard shall be seventy-five (75) feet.
4. No Adult Entertainment Business or Facility shall have any signage or advertisement that encourages, solicits, induces or promotes any conduct or activity proscribed by this Chapter.
(Ord. No. 10-06-07(B), § I, 6-7-2010)
275:
1. No Adult Entertainment Facility shall be located on any parcel not having frontage on the following streets and meeting the following limitation:
a. Any parcel zoned M-1 or M-2 on the east side of Industrial Boulevard from 100 feet south of Ga. Highway 20/81 to 100 feet north of Ga. Highway 155.
b. Any parcel zoned M-1 or M-2 on Park West Drive.
c. City staff in instructed to accept and process any application tendered for an Adult Entertainment Business proposed on any site meeting these limitations pending any necessary revision to the zoning ordinance.
Whenever it shall be recognized by the City Administrator, or suggested by any person, that the above limitations, due to the passage of time and the establishment of adult entertainment businesses, has resulted in an inadequate opportunity for the establishment of subsequent adult entertainment businesses within the allowed numerical and location limitations, they may make such suggestion to the Mayor and Council, in writing, through the City Administrator. In such event, the City Administrator shall investigate the validity of such suggestion, and if it appears to be the case, the City Administrator shall, within 20 days of the suggestion, so report to the Mayor and Council. Thereafter, the Mayor and Council shall, within 20 days thereafter, revise this section so as to allow reasonable opportunities for the establishment of allowable adult entertainment businesses.
(Ord. No. 10-06-07(B), § I, 6-7-2010)
276:
Any License granted pursuant hereto shall be a mere grant or privilege to carry on such business during the term of the License subject to all the terms and conditions imposed by this Chapter and related laws, applicable provisions of this Code and other Ordinances and resolutions of the City relating to such business. All Licenses are subject to be suspended or revoked under the provisions of this Chapters of the City now in effect or which hereafter may be enacted.
(Ord. No. 10-06-07(B), § I, 6-7-2010)
277:
A. No person, group, unincorporated association, firm, partnership, corporation or other entity may operate or conduct an Adult Entertainment Business or offer any form of Adult Entertainment without a valid and current License having first been issued by the City Administrator, except as provided in below when the City Administrator or his designee fails to approve or deny an application for an adult entertainment license within the thirty-day period provided for therein. All applications for licenses hereunder shall be made upon sworn affidavit, and any resulting License shall be valid only if the information contained in the Application therefore is true, correct and complete. In the event [it] is discovered that any of the information contained in the sworn application is not true, correct or complete, it shall be grounds for revocation of any license issued as a result thereof. In no event shall any license issued to an adult entertainment establishment under this Chapter be in force or effect after midnight of December 31 of the year in which it is issued. The issuance of such an annual license shall not be deemed to authorize, condone or make legal any activity there under if the same is deemed illegal or unlawful under the laws of the State of Georgia or the United States.
B. There shall be an annual regulatory fee for each adult entertainment business licensed within the City in an amount established by the City's governing body. The annual regulatory fee must be paid to the City within ten (10) days after the City Administrator or his designee approves the application for an adult entertainment business license or a renewal thereof. No adult entertainment business license or renewal thereof shall be issued until the most recent annual regulatory fee has been paid. All licenses granted hereunder shall expire at midnight on December 31 of the year in which they are issued. Licensees who desire to renew their license shall file an application with the City Administrator or his designee on the form provided for renewal of the license for the ensuing year. Applications for renewal must be filed before November 30 of each year. Any applicant filing a renewal application which is received by the City after November 30 shall pay, in addition to said annual regulatory fee, a late charge of twenty (20) percent, and shall cease conducting business on the premises effective midnight December 31 until a renewal license is duly issued under this Chapter. If a license renewal application is received after January 1, such application shall be treated as an initial application and the applicant shall be required to comply with all rules and regulations for the granting of licenses as if no previous license had been held, and the applicant shall cease conducting business on the premises until a renewal license is duly issued under this Chapter. If a license application is received after January 1, investigative and administrative costs as set forth in this Chapter will be assessed. All licenses granted hereunder shall be for the calendar year and the full annual regulatory fee must be paid for a license renewal application filed prior to July 1 of the license year. One-half (½) of a full annual regulatory fee shall be paid for a license renewal application filed after July 1 of the license year. Any person renewing any license issued hereunder who shall pay the annual regulatory fee, or any portion thereof, after January 1, shall, in addition to said annual regulatory fee and late charges, pay simple interest on the delinquent balance at the annual rate then charged by the Internal Revenue Service of the United States on unpaid federal income taxes.
C. Licenses and permits issued under this Chapter shall not be transferable, except for a license or ownership interest under the following circumstances: in case of the death of an owner or a licensee as defined herein, the license pertaining to the owner's or licensee's adult entertainment establishment shall remain in force and effect for a period of up to thirty (30) days in order to allow the beneficiary (or beneficiaries) who will inherit the ownership interest or license an opportunity to apply for and qualify to hold the interest or license under this Chapter. In order to qualify to hold said interest or license, the beneficiary (or beneficiaries) shall make application to the City within the thirty-day period as if he or she were applying for a new ownership interest or license under this Chapter. If a completed application is filed within the thirty-day period, then the existing license shall remain in effect for an additional period of up to thirty (30) days following the date of filing in order to allow the City Administrator to grant or deny the application under this Chapter. If the City Administrator grants the application, or if the application is deemed granted because of a failure to approve or deny the same within the thirty-day period provided for in this Chapter, then the beneficiary applicant(s) shall become the new owner(s) of the interest or license, which shall be considered transferred without any interruption of ownership interest and without any loss of vested rights, if any, which may have existed from the original approval of same, said interest or license being thereafter subject to all of the terms and conditions of this Chapter. If the beneficiary fails to file a completed application under this subsection within the thirty-day period, or if the application is denied (and if appealed, the denial is upheld on appeal), then the ownership interest or license shall terminate at midnight on the thirtieth day or at midnight on the day that a final judgment upholding the appeal is entered, and the adult entertainment establishment shall close its business on that day; provided, however, that nothing herein shall be construed to allow or permit any license to remain in force and effect beyond midnight on December 31 of the year in which the death occurs, unless necessary to allow for one (1) or both of the two (2) thirty-day periods provided for in this subsection. If an appeal of a denial might remain pending on December 31 of the year in which it is filed, then in such an event, the beneficiary applicant shall file a new application for a license or approval of an ownership interest for the next succeeding calendar year under the terms of this Chapter.
D. All other changes in an ownership interest in an adult entertainment establishment or a license issued under this Chapter must be reported in writing to the City's chief of police or his designee prior to such transfer, and the person who is intended to receive such ownership interest shall be required to make an application for a license as if he or she were applying for a new license hereunder. No licensee may change the location of the licensee's operation; any change in location shall require application for a new license under this Chapter, so that such application process is completed before the relocation takes place.
E. A License to operate an Adult Entertainment Business must be applied for and held in the name of the person, group, unincorporated association, firm, partnership, Limited Liability Company or corporation that actually operates the Business.
F. A separate License shall be required for each Facility of an Adult Entertainment Business.
(Ord. No. 10-06-07(B), § I, 6-7-2010)
280:
A. No person, partnership, business, firm or corporation shall be granted a License if any person, partner, officer or owner of 15% percent or more of the shares of or interest in any such business, firm, partnership or corporation has been convicted or pled guilty or entered a plea of nolo contendere to any crime involving keeping a place of prostitution, pandering, pimping, public indecency, prostitution, sodomy, solicitation of sodomy, masturbation for hire, sexual battery, rape, child molestation, enticing a child for indecent purposes, or any offense included in the definition of a "criminal offense against a victim who is a minor" as defined in O.C.G.A. § 42-1-12 within a period of fifteen (15) years next preceding the date of the application. If there has been any such conviction or plea, then the application shall be denied. For purposes of this Chapter, a conviction or plea of guilty or nolo contendere shall be ignored as to any offense for which the applicant was allowed to avail himself of the Georgia First Offender Act unless the applicant is later adjudicated guilty of having violated the terms of his first offender treatment.
B. Should any such person, partner, or officer of shareholder of a corporation, after a License has been granted, be convicted of or plead guilty or nolo contendere to any such crime, said License shall be subject to suspension and revocation.
C. Withdrawal of an owner, officer or partner or enumerated shareholder, after being convicted or entering a plea of guilty or nolo contendere to the above-enumerated crimes shall not necessarily mitigate against the penalty imposed hereby.
D. Transfer of ownership while an owner, partner, officer or enumerated shareholder is under investigation by any law enforcement agency for any of the above-enumerated crimes or after such person has been convicted of or entered a plea of guilty or nolo contendere shall not necessarily mitigate against the penalty imposed hereunder.
(Ord. No. 10-06-07(B), § I, 6-7-2010)
281:
The following shall be the maximum number of Licenses for Adult Entertainment licenses per 7,000 persons living in the City according to the most recent decennial census of the United States as published by the United States Bureau of the Census (in making this calculation, fractions of the required population minimum shall not be counted toward the establishment of an available license):
1. One License for an Adult Entertainment Business offering on its premises and in the presence of Patrons live Adult Entertainment;
2. One License for an Adult Entertainment Business exhibiting pre-recorded Adult Entertainment films or performances; and
3. One License for an Adult Entertainment Business offering for sale, lease or rental Adult Entertainment goods or materials.
Should an Adult Entertainment Business meet the definition of more than one of the above, then its dominant use shall determine the category for purposes of this Paragraph.
Whenever it shall be recognized by the City Administrator, or suggested by any person, that the release of population counts results in the availability of one or more additional licenses, and it is determined by the City Administrator that one or more additional licenses are available, the City shall publish a notice, one time, advising the public of such, and that applications will be received for a period of 45 days subsequent to the publication.
If, during this period, applications are received which exceed the number of newly available licenses, there shall be held a lottery, administered by City Administrator, to determine the order in which applications shall be processed. Thereafter, the applications shall be processed in the order reflected in the results of the lottery. Once the processing of applications has resulted in the issuance of licenses up to the limit contained in this Chapter, the remaining applications shall be returned to the applicants, unprocessed.
If no applications are received during the forty-five-day period after publication, applications shall thereafter be processed in the order in which they may thereafter be received.
(Ord. No. 10-06-07(B), § I, 6-7-2010)
282:
This Chapter does not license, permit or render legal any act or conduct that is illegal under the laws of the State of Georgia or the United States of America.
(Ord. No. 10-06-07(B), § I, 6-7-2010)
283:
A license to operate an Adult Entertainment Business shall be valid from the date of issuance until January 1, of the following year and must be renewed annually. A change of ownership at any time shall require a new License and a new License Fee.

284:

(Ord. No. 10-06-07(B), § I, 6-7-2010)
285:
Any change in the legal, equitable or beneficial ownership of an Adult Entertainment Business shall require such Business to obtain a new License, including submission of a new License Application, Investigation Fee and License Fee.
(Ord. No. 10-06-07(B), § I, 6-7-2010)
286:
Any person, firm, partnership or corporation which holds an Adult Entertainment Facility license must also comply with all applicable local, state and federal laws or regulations.
(Ord. No. 10-06-07(B), § I, 6-7-2010)
287:
All Applications for new Licenses shall be passed upon by the City Administrator within 30 days of the date of filing of the completed Application. Date of filing shall be the time that a properly completed and executed Application, along with the Investigation Fee, is received by the City Administrator. Upon the expiration of the 30-day period without a decision being made on the Application by the City Administrator, the applicant shall be permitted to begin and conduct business as an Adult Entertainment Business under this statutory provision until such time as the City Administrator acts upon the Application for a new or renewal License. No person or entity conducting business as an Adult Entertainment Business under this provision shall acquire any vested rights to continued conduct of such business, and if the City Administrator later denies the Application, the business must be brought into compliance with this Chapter.

288:
In the event that the City Administrator denies an Application for a license, the denial shall be transmitted in writing, with the reasons for that action specified, to the mailing address specified on the Application and pursuant to the requirements of section 5.08.180.

289:
Qualifications. All employees of an adult entertainment facility shall be not less than eighteen (18) years of age. No employee employed in an adult entertainment facility shall have been convicted of an offense described in section 9-12-5(d)(3) of this Chapter within the five (5) years immediately preceding the proposed employment at or by an adult entertainment facility. Any adult entertainment facility employee who is convicted of any such crimes while so employed shall not thereafter work on any licensed premises in the City for a period of five (5) years from the date of such conviction, unless a longer time is ordered by a court of competent jurisdiction. The terms "licensed premises" and "convicted" are defined in section 9-12-2 of this Chapter.
Permit for employment. Before any person may work as an employee on a licensed premises, he or she shall file a notice with the chief of police or his designee of his or her intended employment on forms supplied by the City and shall thereupon receive a temporary permit for such employment from the chief of police or his designee, which shall expire when the annual permit provided for herein is issued or when the decision of the chief of police or his designee to deny the permit is finally upheld or overturned. The prospective employee shall supply a signed and notarized consent, on forms prescribed by the Georgia Crime Information Center, authorizing the release of his or her criminal records to the City's police department. The prospective employee shall also provide a list of all of his or her convictions of offenses described in section 9-12-5(d)(3) herein (including pleas of nolo contendere) within the past five (5) years. The chief of police or his designee shall approve or deny the permit within fifteen (15) days of the application. If the prospective employee is found to meet the requirements of this subsection (b), and upon payment of the permit fee, the City shall issue a permit approving such employment within forty-eight (48) hours following such approval.
Independent contractors. For the purpose of this Chapter, independent contractors working for an adult entertainment facility shall be considered as employees and shall be required to satisfy the provisions of this Chapter relating to employees of adult entertainment facilities. As used in this Chapter, the terms "employee" and "adult entertainment facility employee" shall include any person who performs any service on the premises of an adult entertainment facility on a full-time, part-time, or contract basis, whether or not the person an employee, an independent contractor, or any other kind of agent, and whether or not said person performs such services only for tips or is paid a salary, wage, or any other type of compensation by the adult entertainment facility. The term "employee" or adult entertainment facility employee" shall not include a person on the premises for the sole purpose of repair or maintenance of the premises, any building or equipment on the premises, or for the delivery of any goods or merchandise to the premises.
A. No person may be employed, whether as an Employee or as an independent contractor, by an Adult Entertainment Business holding a License issued pursuant hereto without first obtaining a work permit from the McDonough Police Department. No person shall be issued a work permit if he or she has, within the preceding ten years, been convicted or pled guilty or entered a plea of nolo contendere to any crime involving keeping a place of prostitution, pandering, pimping, public indecency, prostitution, sodomy, solicitation of sodomy, masturbation for hire, sexual battery, rape, child molestation, enticing a child for indecent purposes, or any offense included in the definition of a "criminal offense against a victim who is a minor" as defined in O.C.G.A. § 42-1-12 within a period of ten (10) years next preceding the date of the application. If there has been any such conviction or plea, then the application shall be denied. For purposes of this Chapter, a conviction or plea of guilty or nolo contendere shall be ignored as to any offense for which the applicant was allowed to avail himself of the Georgia First Offender Act unless the applicant is later adjudicated guilty of having violated the terms of his first offender treatment. A current and valid work letter must be kept on file at the Adult Entertainment Facility where such person performs or is otherwise employed. This sub-section shall apply to performers, entertainers and musicians engaged in temporary work and independent contractors, as well as regular full-time and part-time Employees, regardless of the nature of work performed.
B. The Police Department shall fingerprint all persons applying for a work permit to work for an Adult Entertainment Business and shall determine whether the work permit applicant has a record of conviction, whether by trial verdict, guilty plea or plea of nolo contendere, to any criminal offense listed above. Within 20 days from the date a complete Application is received by the Police Department, the Police Department shall mail (by certified mail, return receipt requested) to the work permit applicant a letter stating whether the applicant is eligible or ineligible for employment by an Adult Entertainment Business according to the criterion set forth herein. If a determination of ineligibility is made, the reason therefore shall be set forth in the letter. Upon the expiration of the 20-day period without a letter regarding eligibility being mailed to the applicant, the applicant shall be permitted to begin employment at an Adult Entertainment Business under this statutory provision unless and until such time as the Police Department mails to the applicant a letter stating that the applicant is ineligible. No applicant employed by an Adult Entertainment Business under this provision shall acquire any vested rights to such continued employment, and if the Police Department later mails to the applicant a letter stating that the applicant is ineligible, the applicant must comply with this Chapter. For the purposes of this section, date of mailing shall be the date on which the letter is posted with the United States Postal Service.
1. A determination of ineligibility may be appealed to the City Administrator. A notice of appeal shall be filed in writing no later than six business days from the date of the letter from the Police Department. Failure to appeal the Police Department's determination within six business days of the letter from the Police Department shall constitute a waiver any appeal rights hereunder. If an appeal is filed, a hearing shall be held not more than 30 days from the date of the written notice of appeal. Upon the expiration of the 30-day period without a hearing, the applicant shall be permitted to begin employment at an Adult Entertainment Business under this statutory provision unless and until such time as the City Administrator sustains or modifies the determination of the Police Department. No applicant employed by an Adult Entertainment Business under this provision shall acquire any vested rights to such continued employment, and if the City Administrator later sustains or modifies the determination of the Police Department, the applicant must comply with this Chapter.
2. The City Administrator may sustain, overrule, or modify the determination of the Police Department. The decision of the City Administrator following the hearing on the matter shall be issued within 30 days of the date of the hearing and shall be final. Upon the expiration of the 30-day period without a decision of the City Administrator being issued on the matter, the applicant shall be permitted to begin employment at an Adult Entertainment Business under this statutory provision unless and until such time as the City Administrator sustains or modifies the decision of the Police Department. No applicant employed at an Adult Entertainment Facility or by an Adult Entertainment Business under this provision shall acquire any vested rights to continued employment at such business, and if the City Administrator later sustains or modifies the determination of the Police Department, the applicant must comply with this Chapter. There shall be no further appeal of the decision of the City Administrator within the City administration.
C. Work permit shall expire 12 months from the date of issuance and it shall be the responsibility of the Employee or independent contractor to see that the work permit is thereafter renewed. It shall be unlawful for an Adult Entertainment Business to allow any person to work or perform on its premises who does not possess a valid work permit. The Adult Entertainment Business must keep a copy of the work permit of each person who works or performs on file at the Adult Entertainment Facility available at the Facility for inspection by City officials at all times.
D. The Mayor and Council may prescribe reasonable fees for work permits and investigations incident thereto.
(Ord. No. 10-06-07(B), § I, 6-7-2010)
290:
Nothing in this Chapter shall be construed as applying to the practice of any profession or occupation licensed by the State of Georgia or a licensing agency recognized by the State of Georgia.
(Ord. No. 10-06-07(B), § I, 6-7-2010)
291:
A. The following shall constitute grounds for the suspension or revocation of Adult Entertainment Business license:
1. Any violation of this Chapter regulating Adult Entertainment Facilities or other Ordinances of the City relating to conduct of the business.
2. Violation of any federal or state law by any owner or Employee arising out of conduct on the licensed premises or otherwise affecting the suitability of such person to engage in Adult Entertainment.
B. Should the City Administrator determine that grounds for the suspension or revocation of a license exist under subsection (A), the City Administrator shall send by first-class mail to the license holder written notice of the license suspension or revocation with a statement of the grounds supporting such action. Such suspension or revocation shall be effective beginning three business days from the date of the notice. Any license holder may request a hearing within ten days of the date of such notice before the City Administrator for the purpose of presenting evidence and asking for reconsideration of such action. Failure to request such reconsideration within ten days of the date of the notice shall result in a waiver of any appeal rights hereunder.
1. If a hearing for reconsideration before the City Administrator is requested, a hearing shall be held not more than 30 days from the date the written notice requesting such hearing is received by the City Administrator. Upon the expiration of the 30 day period without a hearing, the license holder shall be permitted to resume business as an Adult Entertainment Facility or Adult Entertainment Business under this statutory provision unless and until such time as the City Administrator sustains or modifies the original determination. No person or entity conducting business as an Adult Entertainment Facility or Adult Entertainment Business under this provision shall acquire any vested rights to continued conduct of such business, and if the City Administrator later sustains or modifies the original determination, the business must be brought into compliance with this Chapter.
2. The City Administrator may sustain, overrule, or modify the original determination. The decision of the City Administrator following the hearing on the matter shall be issued within 20 days of the date of the hearing and shall be final. Upon the expiration of the 20-day period without a decision of the City Administrator being issued on the matter, the license holder shall be permitted to resume business as an Adult Entertainment Facility or Adult Entertainment Business under this statutory provision unless and until such time as the City Administrator sustains the original determination. No person or entity conducting business as an Adult Entertainment Facility or Adult Entertainment Business under this provision shall acquire any vested rights to continued conduct of such business, and if the City Administrator later sustains or modifies the original determination, the business must be brought into compliance with this Chapter.
C. Any violation by an Agent or Employee of a License holder which would subject the licensee to suspension or revocation under subsection (A) shall be considered a violation by the licensee for the purpose of the suspension and revocation provisions of this section.
D. In addition to the procedure for license suspension and/or revocation as outlined in the preceding subsections of this section, any violation of this Chapter shall subject the offender, upon conviction, to punishment as provided by Section 1.08.010 of this Code.
(Ord. No. 10-06-07(B), § I, 6-7-2010)
292:
All Adult Entertainment Businesses in existence when this Chapter is enacted shall within 30 (thirty) days of adoption of this Chapter make Application for a License and comply with all the provisions of this Chapter, except as to Permitted Locations (§ 5.08.040), Other Location and Structural Requirements (§ 5.08.050) and Distance Requirements for Location (§ 5.08.060), and shall obtain a License immediately upon notification of approval of License Application. Any Adult Entertainment Business in existence when this Chapter is enacted that is denied a License shall cease and desist all business operations regulated by this Chapter immediately upon notice that its Application has been denied.
(Ord. No. 10-06-07(B), § I, 6-7-2010)
293:
Any adult entertainment facility operated, conducted or maintained contrary to the provisions of this Chapter shall be and the same is hereby declared to be unlawful and a public nuisance. The City may, in addition to or in lieu of prosecuting a criminal action hereunder, commence an action or actions, proceeding or proceedings for abatement, removal or enjoinment thereof in the manner provided by law. It may take such other steps and shall apply to such court or courts as may have jurisdiction to grant such relief as will abate or remove such adult entertainment facility and restrain and enjoin any person from operating, engaging in, conducting or carrying on an adult entertainment facility contrary to the provisions of this Chapter.
(Ord. No. 10-06-07(B), § I, 6-7-2010)
295:
Pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-6-93 there is levied for the year 1984, and for each year thereafter, an annual business license tax upon state and national banking associations, federal savings and loan associations, state building and loan associations a business license tax at the rate of .25 percent of the gross receipts of the institutions as defined. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Chapter, the minimum amount of business license tax due from any depository financial institutions pursuant to this Chapter shall be $1,000.00 per year.
(Prior Code § 13-41; Ord. of 11-7-1983, (part))
297:
A. For the purposes of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply:
Alcohol means ethyl alcohol, hydrated oxide of ethyl, or spirits of wine, and from whatever source or by whatever process produced.
Alcoholic beverage means and includes all alcohol, distilled spirits, beer, malt beverage, wine, or fortified wine intended for human consumption.
Bar or tavern means any premises at which a licensed retailer derives 75% or more total annual gross revenue from the sale of alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises.
Bona fide private club means any nonprofit association organized under the laws of the state meeting all of the following criteria:
1. In existence at least one year prior to the filing of its application for a license to be issued pursuant to this chapter.
2. At least 75 regular dues-paying members.
3. Owns, hires, or leases a building or space within a building for the reasonable use of its members, that has:
a. A suitable kitchen and dining room space and equipment.
b. Sufficient employees for cooking, preparing, and serving meals for its members and guests.
4. No member, officer, agent, or employee may directly or indirectly receive, in the form of salary or other compensation, any profits from the sale of alcoholic beverages beyond a fixed salary.
Brewpub means any eating establishment in which beer or malt beverages are manufactured or brewed, subject to the barrel production limitation prescribed in O.C.G.A. § 3-5-36.
Brownbagging means the bringing, taking or carrying of any alcoholic beverage into a business lawfully operating within the city but not licensed for the consumption of alcoholic beverages on the premises, with the intent to consume such alcoholic beverage on the premises, or the taking of any alcoholic beverage into premises licensed for the sale of alcoholic beverages during such times the sale or consumption of such beverages is prohibited by law; provided that bringing an alcoholic beverage into a house, apartment, room or other unit designed for private residential occupancy for consumption by the residents and invited guests thereof shall not fall within this definition.
Craft beer, as defined by the Brewers Association, Boulder, Colorado, the trade organization for the craft beer/microbrewing industry, are beers (a form of malt beverage) produced by a small, independent brewer who follows traditional brewing processes using select, sometimes non-traditional, ingredients to produce a distinctive product. Craft brewers produce very limited annual quantities, much less than traditional breweries that produce millions of barrels per year.
Distilled spirits means any alcoholic beverage obtained by distillation or containing more than 21% alcohol by volume, including, but not limited to, all fortified wines.
Eating establishment means an establishment open to the public which is licensed to sell distilled spirits, malt beverages, and/or wines for consumption on the premises and which derives at least 50% of its total annual gross food and beverage sales from the sale of prepared meals or food as its principal business purpose. In order to be licensed for consumption of alcoholic beverages on the premises under this chapter, eating establishments are expected to keep and maintain regular days and hours of operation, at least four (4) days per week, as a convenience to the public, other than holidays, vacations, and periods when closed for repairs or remodeling. When determining the total annual gross food and beverage sales for eating establishments operating as a brewpub, barrels of malt beverages sold to licensed wholesale dealers, or packaged in bottles or growlers sold to the public for consumption off the premises, shall not be used.
Fortified wine means any alcoholic beverage containing more than 21% alcohol by volume made from fruits, berries or grapes, either by natural fermentation or by natural fermentation with brandy added. This term includes, but is not limited to, brandy.
Growler means a bottle, container or vessel, with a capacity of at least 32 ounces and not exceeding 64 ounces that is designed for and especially intended to be filled with a craft beer from a keg by a licensee, or employee of a licensee, holding an eating establishment, brewpub, hotel, or bar license for on premises consumption issued pursuant to this chapter, or a specialty package retailer. A refilled growler that has been properly sealed shall be considered an "unbroken package" for purposes of this chapter.
Hotel means any lodge, inn, or similar establishment which offers overnight sleeping accommodations to registered guests for hire, and at which one or more prepared meals or food are regularly served daily and consumed in one or more dining rooms, having an adequate and sanitary kitchen, such sleeping accommodations and dining rooms being conducted on the same premises. Hotels may grant franchises for the operation of an eating establishment and lounge on their premises, and the holder of such franchise shall be included in this definition of hotel. Lounges may be located separately from dining facilities in hotels provided there is a commonality of ownership of the eating establishment and lounge.
Licensed alcoholic beverage caterer means any Georgia retail dealer licensed, either for package sales or on-premises consumption of alcoholic beverages, who additionally holds a valid license from a county or municipality to sell distilled spirits, malt beverages, or wine for consumption off-premises at authorized catered events.
Lounge means a separate room adjacent to and under common ownership with an eating establishment in which alcoholic beverages may be sold by the drink for consumption on the premises. Except in the case of a bona fide private club or hotel, as defined in this section, a lounge shall be part of the eating establishment, as defined in this section, and shall be interconnected by a doorway opening into the dining area of the eating establishment.
Malt beverage means any alcoholic beverage obtained by the fermentation of any infusion or decoction of barley, malt, hops, or any other similar product, or any combination of such products in water, containing not more than six percent alcohol by volume and including ale, porter, brown, stout, lager beer, small beer, and strong beer. The term does not include sake, known as Japanese rice wine.
Manufacturer means any maker, producer, or bottler of an alcoholic beverage. The term also means: in the case of distilled spirits, any person engaged in distilling, rectifying, or blending any distilled spirits; in the case of malt beverages, any brewer; and, in the case of wine, any vintner.
Package means a bottle, can, keg, barrel, or other original consumer container.
Person means any individual, firm, partnership, cooperative, nonprofit membership corporation, joint venture, association, company, corporation, agency, syndicate, estate, trust, business trust, receiver, fiduciary, or other group or combination acting as a unit, body politic, or political subdivision, whether public, private, or quasi-public.
Premises means the definite closed or partitioned-in locality, whether room, shop or building, wherein alcoholic beverages are sold or consumed. Premises also includes any area or patio immediately adjacent to the main licensed facility and located on property owned or leased by such licensee. The area or patio need not be covered, but must be completely enclosed, except for entrances and exits, by a wall, fence, shrubbery or other decorative material no less than 30 inches in height, and subject to approval, in advance by the Community Development Director.
Proper identification means any document issued by a government agency containing a description of the person and such person's photograph, and giving the person's date of birth; proper identification includes, but is not limited to, a passport, military identification card, driver's license, or identification card issued under O.C.G.A. §§ 40-5-100 through 40-5-104. Proper identification shall not include a birth certificate.
Public club means an establishment, other than an "eating establishment" or a "bar" as defined in this chapter, having the principle purpose of offering live music, dancing, theatrical productions or comedians, and at which the consumption on-premises of alcoholic beverages is incidental. A public club shall not be operated or conducted in conjunction with any other mercantile business, trade or profession, and may offer and sell only those items commonly associated with such establishments.
Retail consumption dealer means any person who sells distilled spirits for consumption on the premises at retail only to consumers and not for resale.
Retailer or retail dealer means, except as to distilled spirits, any person who sells alcoholic beverages, either in unbroken packages or for consumption on the premises, at retail only to consumers and not for resale.
Wholesaler or wholesale dealer means any person who sells alcoholic beverages to other wholesale dealers, to retail dealers, or to retail consumption dealers.
Wine means any alcoholic beverage containing not more than 21% alcohol by volume made from fruits, berries, or grapes either by natural fermentation or by natural fermentation with brandy added. The term includes, but is not limited to, all sparkling wines, champagnes, combinations of such beverages, vermouths, special natural wines, rectified wines, and like products. The term does not include cooking wine mixed with salt or other ingredients so as to render it unfit for human consumption. A liquid shall be first deemed to be a wine at that point in the manufacturing process when it conforms to the definition of wine contained in this section.

A. All holders of licenses under this section must open for business the establishment referred to in the license within 3 months after issuance of the license. Failure to open the licensed establishment within such time shall automatically forfeit and cancel the unused license, and no refund of license fees shall be made to the license holder.
B. Any holder of a license under this article who shall begin the operation of the business as authorized in the license, but who shall cease to operate the business as authorized in the license for a period of 3 consecutive months, shall automatically forfeit his license. Such license shall, by virtue of such failure to operate, be canceled by the City Administrator.
(Ord. No. 17-06-19(C), § 1, 6-19-2017)
338:
A. All licenses granted under this article shall expire on December 31 of each year. Licensees who desire to renew their license shall file a renewal application with the Alcohol Licensing Clerk no later than November 1 of the current year.
B. Annual renewal fees must be paid, in full, pursuant to the following timeline (whichever date shall come first):
1. December 31 of the current year;
2. In the event December 31 falls on a Saturday or Sunday, then no later than 12 noon on the last Friday in December of the current year; or
3. At the time of issuance of a renewal license.
Payment of annual renewal fees shall be tendered in cash or cash equivalent to the Alcohol Licensing Clerk. No other form of payment shall be accepted.
C. Any person renewing any license issued under this article who shall pay the required fee, or any portion thereof, after the date set for such payment shall, in addition to such annual fee, pay a late payment penalties as follows: for retail package sales—$100; for manufacturers or wholesalers—$25; for on-premises (malt-beverages/wine)—$200; for on-premises (all alcoholic beverages)—$375; for all other licenses—10% of the annual license fee.
(Ord. No. 17-06-19(C), § 1, 6-19-2017)
339:
A. No license for the sale of alcoholic beverages shall be transferable except as otherwise provided in this section.
B. Any person seeking the transfer of an existing license for the sale of alcoholic beverages must first submit a written transfer application on a form prescribed by the City Administrator, along with a non-refundable investigation fee in the amount of $100.00.
C. In no event shall any license be transferable if there are any fees, taxes, or other revenues due to the city by the former licensee.
D. Eligibility. Transfer of an existing license is discretionary and may be allowed in the following limited circumstances:
1. Death. In case of the death of a licensee, the licensed establishment shall be allowed to continue to sell alcoholic beverages for a period of 45 days from the date of death, or until expiration of the license, or until approval of a new licensee, whichever shall first occur. However, no sale of alcoholic beverages shall be allowed until such time as a personal representative of the estate, appointed by a probate court of competent jurisdiction, has submitted the transfer application required by this section.
2. Relocation. If a licensee seeks to move his place of business from the licensed premises to another place within the city, the licensee must submit a transfer application no later than 60 days prior to the anticipated date of relocation. Should a transfer of location be approved, with no change of ownership of the business, a new license fee shall not be required for the remainder of the license year.
3. Change in ownership; partnerships and corporations. Prior approval by the City Administrator shall not be required where 1 or more of the partners in a licensed partnership withdraws in favor of 1 or more of the partners who were partners at the time of the issuance of the license. Further, prior approval by the City Administrator shall not be required for the transfer of stock between persons who held stock in the corporate owner at the time of issuance of the license; nor shall prior approval be required for transfers of stock that do not result in any person increasing his stock holdings to a total of 10% or more of any class of stock.
4. Change in ownership; sale of business. In the event of a sale of a licensed business, or if a license is surrendered or a licensee severs his association with a licensed establishment, the purchaser or licensee's successor may continue to sell alcoholic beverages for a period of 45 days from the date of sale, surrender or severance only if the following conditions are met:
a. Prior to the date of closing on the sale of the business, surrender or severance, the purchaser or licensee's successor shall submit a new application for a license together with the $100.00 investigative fee.
b. Compliance with all other relevant conditions and requirements under state and local law.
Upon issuance of a new license, the authorization to sell under the previous license shall be revoked by operation of law. No additional license fees shall be required during the period for which the original license was issued.
(Ord. No. 17-06-19(C), § 1, 6-19-2017)
340:
A. Except as provided in section 5.24.230 above, any change in the ownership of any entity owning a licensed establishment shall automatically cancel and revoke any license issued under this chapter without the necessity of any hearing.
B. Violation of this section or section 5.24.230, above, shall result in revocation of the license being used and a fine on the new ownership and the old ownership of $500.00. No license will be issued to the old or the new owner in the city for 1 year from the date of the violation.
(Ord. No. 17-06-19(C), § 1, 6-19-2017)
342:
A. Any bona fide nonprofit civic organization may be issued a temporary permit to sell alcoholic beverages for consumption only on the premises for a period not to exceed 1 day. The nonprofit civic organization must make application and pay a fee of $25.00.
B. No more than 2 permits may be issued to an organization in any one 1-calendar year.
C. Such civic organizations shall be required to comply with all ordinance regulations dealing with general licensing and consumption on the premises' establishments.
(Ord. No. 17-06-19(C), § 1, 6-19-2017)
343:
A. Eligibility for license to sell or distribute by the drink off-premises; application; fee.
1. Any holder of a city license authorizing the licensee to sell beer, malt beverages, or wine by the drink for consumption on the premises may apply for an off-premises license as an alcoholic beverage caterer to sell or distribute beer, malt beverages, or wine by the drink off premises and in connection with an authorized catered function.
2. Any holder of a city license authorizing the licensee to sell beer, malt beverages, or wine by the package for consumption off the premises may apply for an off-premises license as on alcoholic beverage caterer to sell or distribute beer, malt beverages, or wine by the drink off premises and in connection with an authorized catered function.
3. Any holder of a city license authorizing the licensee to sell distilled spirits by the drink for consumption on the premises may apply for an off-premises license as an alcoholic beverage caterer to sell or distribute distilled spirits by the drink off-premises and in connection with an authorized catered function.
4. Each application for a license as an alcoholic beverage caterer shall be accompanied by a certified check for the full amount of the license fee.
B. Authorized catered functions; event permits.
1. In order to distribute or sell distilled spirits, malt beverages, or wine at a catered function, the licensed alcoholic beverage caterer shall be required to apply to the city clerk for an event permit. The application shall include the name of the caterer; the date, address, and time of the event; and the alcoholic beverage caterer's license number.
2. When an alcoholic beverage caterer is domiciled outside the City and currently licensed by the local government authority in which it is domiciled as on alcoholic beverage caterer, a City license shall not be required in order for the alcoholic beverage caterer to distribute or sell distilled spirits, malt beverages, or wine at a catered function inside the city. However, an event fee of fifty dollars ($50.00) shall be charged by the city and local excise taxes shall be levied on the total quantity of alcoholic beverages brought into the city by the caterer. A copy of the license issued by the local government authority where the alcoholic beverage caterer is domiciled shall be attached to the event application.
C. Hours of sale.
1. Licensed alcoholic beverage caterers may not distribute or sell distilled spirits, beer, malt beverages, or wine for off-premises consumption except between the hours of 9:00 a.m. and 11:55 p.m., Monday through Saturday, and the 2 hours immediately following such time, i.e., until 1:55 a.m. on the subsequent day.
2. Licensed alcoholic beverage caterers who derive a minimum of 50% of their total annual gross food and beverage sales from the sale of prepared meals or food may sell and serve alcoholic beverages for off-premises consumption on Sundays between the hours of 12:30 p.m. and 12:00 midnight. Such alcoholic beverage caterers must complete a form and affidavit furnished by the City and certify the percentages for the most recently ended fiscal year. For new establishments, no affidavit shall be required and such establishments shall be allowed 6 months to comply with the 50% rule.
3. Any alcoholic beverage served must be consumed within 30 minutes of the required closing.
(Ord. No. 17-06-19(C), § 1, 6-19-2017)
344:
A. An ancillary tasting license may be issued in conjunction with a retail consumption license for alcoholic beverages, including brewpubs, or a retail package license for malt beverages and/or wine only, and a valid current license from the state.
B. No tasting shall be conducted on the premises of any place of business licensed to sell distilled spirits in the unbroken package.
C. A tasting license shall allow the licensee to offer malt beverage or wine samples in connection with an educational or appreciation class. A tasting license is intended to allow such activity on a limited basis and shall not be a part of the core operations of such establishment. Such events shall be limited to no more than six per week and shall not exceed two consecutive hours in length. No more than three classes may be held in any consecutive 24-hour period.
D. A tasting licensee shall be subject to all laws, rules and regulations of the city and state, and shall be subject to license revocation for violation thereof.
E. Licensees shall be subject to the following restrictions:
1. No customer shall receive more than eighteen ounces of wine from the licensee per class, and the licensee shall not serve any individual portion that exceeds three ounces.
2. No customer shall receive more than 32 ounces of malt beverage from the licensee per class, and the licensee shall not serve any individual portion that exceeds eight ounces.
3. Only the licensee or an agent thereof shall open, handle, and serve opened packages or bottles of wine, and individual samples shall only be poured by the licensee or an employee thereof.
4. Customers shall not remove opened packages or unsealed bottles from the premises.
5. Customers may not attend more than one class in a single day.
6. The educational and appreciation classes shall consist of at least one hour of lecture on craft malt beverages or wines, including a lecture on responsible alcohol consumption.
7. Tasting licensees are prohibited from conducting tastings at any location where motor fuel is sold or dispensed. No ancillary tasting license shall be granted to any retail package dealer in distilled spirits.
8. Attendance at classes may be limited on a "first come" basis and reasonably restricted to available seating space.
9. No licensee shall charge more than $20.00 for a person to attend a class, inclusive of the cost of the malt beverage or wine sampled at the event, unless the event is held as a fundraiser for a charity or nonprofit cause. If held for charitable purposes, the licensee shall conspicuously display a sign at the event identifying the name of the charity and provide a written receipt. Records shall be maintained showing the amount raised, the cost of putting on the event, and the actual amount remitted to the charity.
(Ord. No. 17-06-19(C), § 1, 6-19-2017)
346:
A. Except as otherwise provided in this chapter, no license shall be suspended or revoked except for due cause and after hearing, upon not less than three (3) days prior written notice to the holder of the license of the time, place and purpose of the hearing and a statement of the charges upon which the hearing shall be held.
B. "Due cause" for the purposes of this section shall include, but not be limited to:
1. Conviction of, or the entering of a plea of guilty or nolo contendere by, the licensee or any of his or her employees or any person holding an interest in the license for any felony, any law, administrative regulation or ordinance involving alcoholic beverages, gambling or narcotics, or tax laws.
2. Conviction of, or the entering of a plea of guilty or nolo contendere by, the licensee or any of his or her employees or any person holding an interest in the license for any sex offense when the business is licensed for on-premise consumption;
3. Suspension or revocation of any state license required as a condition for the possession, sale or distribution of alcoholic beverages;
4. Material falsification of any fact given in an application for a license issued under this chapter or bearing upon the licensee's qualification therefor; any act which may be construed as a subterfuge in an effort to circumvent any of the qualifications for a license under this chapter shall be deemed a violation of the requirement attempted to be circumvented;
5. Failure to meet or maintain any standard prescribed by this chapter as a condition or qualification for holding a license;
6. Any other factor known to or discovered by the City whereby it is objectively shown the licensee, any of the licensee's employees or any person holding an interest in a license, has engaged in conduct at or involving the licensed business or has permitted conduct on the licensed premises that constitutes a violation of federal or state law, local ordinance, or administrative regulations involving alcoholic beverages, gambling, narcotics, or disorderly conduct, including any sexual offense, under state law or local ordinances with respect to businesses licensed for on-premise consumption.
a) With respect to this section, it shall be presumed that the violation was done with the knowledge or consent of the licensee.
b) Provided, however, such presumption may be rebutted only by evidence which precludes every other reasonable hypothesis save that such licensee did not know, assist or aid in such occurrence, or in the exercise of full diligence that such licensee could not have discovered or prevented such activity.
C. Notice of suspension or revocation proceedings shall be served on the person named as licensee in the application. Notice shall be in writing. The notice may be served personally or by statutory overnight delivery. If by statutory overnight delivery, the notice shall be addressed to the licensee at its street address as it appears in the records of the city. The burden shall be on the licensee to provide notice, in writing, of any change of street address for service of notices and process. In the case of service by statutory overnight delivery of any notice required by this chapter, the service is deemed complete at the time of deposit with the statutory overnight provider.
D. The hearing shall be conducted by the mayor and council, with the mayor presiding. Hearings shall be only as formal as necessary to preserve order and shall be compatible with the principles of justice. The city attorney shall present the city's case and bear the burden of proving by a preponderance of the evidence that due cause exists to suspend or revoke the license. At the hearing the licensee shall have the right to represent itself or be represented by counsel, may cross-examine all witnesses offered by the city, and may call witnesses and present evidence in its own behalf. Formal rules of evidence shall not apply to hearings under this section, although the mayor shall have the right to exclude evidence which carries no indicia of reliability. All testimony shall be offered under oath or affirmation.
E. The mayor and council shall make its final determination within 10 days of the completion of the hearing. The decision shall be placed in writing and contain the mayor and council's findings of fact, conclusions of law, and decision as to penalty, if any. Such penalty may include one or more of the following: revocation of the license; suspension of the license for no more than twelve (12) months; imposition of a probationary period not to exceed twelve (12) months, and/or a civil penalty for a first offense not to exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) and for second and subsequent offenses, not to exceed five thousand dollars ($5,000.00). Where a probationary period is imposed which exceeds the term of the current license, the mayor and council may provide provisional conditions for a renewal license.
F. The mayor and council's decision shall be personally served upon the licensee or mailed by first class mail to the licensee's attorney and city attorney within 10 days of the close of the hearing. Action taken by the mayor and council following the hearing shall be final.
(Ord. No. 17-06-19(C), § 1, 6-19-2017)
347:

(Ord. No. 17-06-19(C), § 1, 6-19-2017)
348:
A. The city administrator has authority to suspend a license for a short-term period not to exceed ten (10) days. The city administrator's decision shall be in writing, with the term of the suspension and the reasons therefor stated, and shall be mailed or delivered to the licensee as provided in Section 5.24.250.
B. A short-term suspension by the city administrator must be for an emergency cause. "Emergency cause" for the short-term suspension of a license shall consist of a third or subsequent violation by the same licensee or the licensee's employees or agents on the same premises within a two-year period of any state or federal laws, administrative regulations of the state or city ordinances regulating such business holding a license, including those prohibiting gambling, regulating the sale, manufacture, distribution, handling, dealing in, and possession of alcoholic beverages, including the sale or transfer of alcoholic beverages to minors in an unlawful manner, and the manufacture, sale, or distribution of any controlled substance which puts the city and the health and safety of its citizens at such risk that an immediate suspension is necessary until a hearing as provided for in Section 5.24.250 can be held.

349:
The mayor and council is authorized to suspend the sale of alcoholic beverages under all licenses issued pursuant to this chapter during any state of emergency declared by the Governor, any local emergency as defined by O.C.G.A. § 36-69-2 or for any other serious situation in which the mayor and council deems such emergency suspension necessary for the protection of the health and welfare of the citizens of the City of McDonough. 350:

(Ord. No. 17-06-19(C), § 1, 6-19-2017)
353:
A. Retail package sales of malt beverages or wine. Sales are permitted, Monday through Saturday, including election days, 12:01 a.m.—11:45 p.m.; provided, however, it shall be unlawful for any person to sell alcoholic beverages within two hundred fifty (250) feet of any polling place or of the outer edge of any building within which such polling place is established during the hours the polls are open. Monday through Saturday, including election days: 11:00 a.m.—2:00 a.m.; provided, however, it shall be unlawful for any person to sell alcoholic beverages from premises located within two hundred fifty (250) feet of any polling place or of the outer edge of any building within which such polling place is established during the hours the polls are open. 354:

These inspections shall be made for the purpose of verifying compliance with the requirements of this chapter and state law. This section is not intended to limit the authority of any other city official to conduct inspections authorized by other provisions of the City Code.

355:
A. All retail establishments licensed to sell alcoholic beverages shall post in a conspicuous place a notice which shall contain the provisions of the laws of this state which deal with the unlawful sole of such items to minors and the penalties for violating such laws.
B. All retail consumption dealers and retail dealers who sell at retail any alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises shall post, in a conspicuous place, a sign which clearly reads: "Warning: Drinking alcoholic beverages during pregnancy can cause birth defects."
C. The state department of revenue shall make such signs available to such retailers of alcoholic beverages and shall promulgate rules and regulations with respect to the form and the posting of such signs.

356:
A. No person, knowingly and intentionally, may sell or offer to sell:
1. Any wine or malt beverages within 100 yards of any school building, school grounds, or college campus. This subparagraph shall not apply at any location for which a license has been issued prior to July 1, 1981, nor to the renewal of such license. Nor shall this subparagraph apply at any location for which a new license is applied for if the sale of wine and beer was lawful at such location at any time during the 12 months immediately preceding such application.
2. Any distilled spirits in or within 100 yards of any church building or within 200 yards of any school building, educational building, school grounds, or college campus.
3. Any distilled spirits, wine, or malt beverages within 100 yards of an alcoholic treatment center owned and operated by the state, county or City. This paragraph shall not apply to any business having a license in effect on July 1, 1981.
B. As used in this subsection, the term "school building" or "educational building" shall apply only to state, county, city, or church school buildings and to such buildings at such other schools in which are taught subjects commonly taught in the common schools and colleges of this state and which are public schools or private schools as defined in subsection (b) of O.C.G.A. § 20-2-690.
C. For the purpose of this section, distance shall be measured by the most direct route of travel on the ground. No license in effect as of the enactment of this chapter shall be revoked before its date of expiration, or renewal denied by reason of the method of measurement set out in this section, if the license was granted in reliance on another method of measurement.
D. On-premise consumption licensees. Licensees for the sale of alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises are not subject to the location restrictions in subparagraphs (1) and (2); however, licensees for on premises consumption shall be subject to the restrictions in subparagraph (3).
E. Housing Authorities.
1. As used in this subsection, the term "housing authority property" means any property containing 300 housing units or fewer owned or operated by a housing authority created under state law.
2. No person knowingly and intentionally may sell any alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises within 100 yards of any housing authority property. This subsection shall not apply at any location for which a license has been issued prior to July 1, 2000, nor to the renewal of such license. Nor shall this subsection apply at any location for which a new license is applied for if the sale of alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises was lawful at such location at any time during the 12 months immediately preceding such application.
F. No licenses shall be issued to any location unless the location has been zoned commercial.
(Ord. No. 17-06-19(C), § 1, 6-19-2017)
358:
No retailer shall purchase alcoholic beverages from any person, firm or corporation other than a wholesaler licensed under this chapter. No wholesaler shall sell any alcoholic beverages to anyone other than a retailer licensed under this chapter.

359:
A. As used in this section, "open container," means any container, containing alcoholic beverages, which is immediately capable of being consumed from or the seal of which has been broken.
B. No person shall possess an open container of any alcoholic beverage within the passenger compartment of a motor vehicle. Closed containers of alcoholic beverages may lawfully be transported in any part of a vehicle. Open containers shall be placed in a locked glove box, locked trunk or locked storage container.
C. No person shall possess an open container of any alcoholic beverage while walking, standing or otherwise occupying any public street, road, or highway, sidewalk adjacent thereto, public parking lot, park or other publicly owned properties of the City; provided that where the Mayor and Council has approved a public building, location or facility as one where alcoholic beverages may be consumed and has posted a sign authorizing such use, this section shall not apply to the otherwise lawful possession and consumption of alcoholic beverages in the area so designated.
D. No person shall possess an open container of or consume any alcoholic beverage on the premises of any package dealer, including parking lots adjacent thereto. This section shall not apply with respect to: (i) tastings provided pursuant to an ancillary tasting license; (ii) sales pursuant to a license for consumption on the premises; or (iii) duly licensed brewers and brewpubs operating in compliance with the state law.
E. No person shall enter or leave the premises of any dealer licensed to sell or dispense alcoholic beverages for on-premise consumption with an open container of any alcoholic beverage.
(Ord. No. 17-06-19(C), § 1, 6-19-2017)
360:
Brownbagging, as defined in this chapter, is prohibited within the City. Any person who brownbags, participates in consumption of any alcoholic beverage being brownbagged, or any licensee or employee of a licensed establishment in whose presence brownbagging knowingly or with reckless indifference occurs, shall be in violation of this section.
(Ord. No. 17-06-19(C), § 1, 6-19-2017)
361:
All package dealers and on-premise consumption dealers shall store all alcoholic beverages on the premises for which the license was issued and at no other place. All stock shall be available at all times for inspection by any duly authorized representative of the City. Any alcoholic beverages found in any licensee's stock which was not sold or distributed by a wholesaler licensed in accordance with laws of Georgia to make sales and deliveries in the City shall be subject to immediate confiscation. No licensee shall keep, possess or store at such licensee's place of business any alcoholic beverage for which such licensee does not hold a valid and current State and local license to sell such alcoholic beverage.
(Ord. No. 17-06-19(C), § 1, 6-19-2017)
362:
A. No licensee shall permit any employee under the age of 18 to dispense, serve, sell, or take orders for alcoholic beverages; provided, however, this provision shall not prohibit employees under the age of 18 who are employed in grocery stores, discount/general merchandise department stores, convenience stores, or drugstores from handling or carrying sealed packages of alcoholic beverages either within the licensed premises or to customers' vehicles when parked adjacent thereto as a part of employment responsibilities so long as such employees under age 18 do not dispense, serve, sell, or take orders for any alcoholic beverage.
B. No licensee under this chapter shall permit any person to sell, dispense, serve or take orders for alcoholic beverages while that person is currently serving a sentence, including probation or parole, based upon a conviction in any state or federal court or the United States or in any foreign country for any felony, or any misdemeanor ordinance violating relating to the manufacture, sale, use or distribution of alcoholic beverages or narcotics or controlled substances, gambling, sexual offenses, or crimes of moral turpitude. No licensee shall employ within its business for the purpose of selling or dispensing alcoholic beverages any person convicted within five years immediately prior to the application for employment of any felony or within two years immediately prior to the application for employment of any misdemeanor or ordinance violation relating to the manufacture, sale, use or distribution of alcoholic beverages or narcotics or controlled substances, gambling, sexual offenses, or a crime of moral turpitude. This provision shall not prohibit employees who have been convicted or have a criminal history, when employed in supermarkets, convenience stores or drugstores, from handling or carrying alcoholic beverages either within the licensed premises or to customers' vehicles when parked adjacent thereto as a part of employment responsibilities.

It shall be the duty of the licensee to train all employees whose duties shall include the sale, dispensing, serving or taking of orders for alcoholic beverages in the requirements of this chapter and applicable state laws and regulations. Each licensee shall establish written policies, a copy of which shall be posted within the licensed premises, governing the sole and dispensing of alcoholic beverages in accordance with state law and this chapter. Licensees are encouraged to adopt disciplinary sanctions for employees who fail to meet the standards of law as violations by employees may constitute grounds for revocation, suspension or denial of a license under this chapter. The degree of training, supervision and discipline of employees by the licensee may be considered by the hearing officer in determining action on any license.
(Ord. No. 17-06-19(C), § 1, 6-19-2017)
363:
(a) Except for the area and circumstances specified in subsection (b) herein, it shall be unlawful for any person to possess an alcoholic beverage in an open container, either on their person, in a motor vehicle, or otherwise, on the streets, sidewalks, parks, or other public places within the City of McDonough.

364:
Except as otherwise provided, it shall be unlawful for any person to sell, serve, or otherwise dispense any alcoholic beverage in a street, alley, or parking lot commonly used by the public or in any other public place or on public property.
(Ord. No. 17-06-19(C), § 1, 6-19-2017)
366:
A. No package dealer shall operate such business in connection with any other mercantile establishment, except that a package dealer may sell or display or keep in stock for retail sale the following inventory:
1. Distilled spirits, wines, malt beverages, provided the dealer is separately licensed for each.
2. Tobacco products, limited to tobacco, cigarettes, cigars, chewing tobacco, snuff, cigarette papers, lighters and matches which do not carry or refer to the name of any licensed dealer or the location of his place of business.
